title: How major US stock indexes fared Monday 10/19/2026
detail:
How major US stock indexes fared Monday 10/19/2026
The Associated Press
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 3:20 PM CDT 1 min read
^GSPC
^DJI
^RUT
^IXIC

AI stocks recovered some of their steep losses from last week, but the rest of the market and stocks worldwide were shaky.

The S&P 500 rose 0.4% Monday, and the Nasdaq composite rallied 1.1%. The majority of U.S. stocks outside of AI and tech fell, though, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average closed 0.1% lower after swinging between losses and gains earlier in the day.

In Europe, indexes fell more than 1% following protests over the weekend that could force governments to increase their spending. Yields cranked higher in bond markets worldwide.

On Monday:

The S&P 500 rose 31.29 points, or 0.4%, to 7,690.73.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 36.38 points, or 0.1%, to 51,966.03.

The Nasdaq composite rose 290.85 points, or 1.1%, to 26,430.89.

The Russell 2000 index of smaller companies rose 6.93 points, or 0.3%, to 2,728.30.

For the year:

The S&P 500 is up 845.23 points, or 12.3%.

The Dow is up 3,902.74 points, or 8.1%.

The Nasdaq is up 3,188.90 points, or 13.7%.

The Russell 2000 is up 246.39 points, or 9.9%.

title: Update: Technology, Consumer Discretionary Lift US Equity Indexes While Treasury Yields Climb
detail:
PREMIUM
Update: Technology, Consumer Discretionary Lift US Equity Indexes While Treasury Yields Climb
MT Newswires
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 2:51 PM CDT 1 min read
^GSPC
^DJI
^IXIC

(Updates with index/price moves from the first paragraph.)

US equity indexes rose amid gains in consumer discretionary and technology ahead of Monday's close, while government bond yields rose.

The Nasdaq Composite jumped 1.3% to 26,490.4, the S&P 500 advanced 0.6% to 7,705.4, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed less than 0.1% to 52,045.6 in the final leg. Utilities and real estate led decliners.

The iShares PHLX Semiconductor Exchange Traded Fund (SOXX), with about $48.43 billion in assets under management, jumped 2.5%, the first gain in 10 days.

Eighteen of the top 20 stocks in a category with market capitalization exceeding $200 billion were from the technology sector, according to data compiled by Finviz. Most top gainers in this mega-cap category were from the semiconductor or related industries.

Most US Treasury yields rose as last week's AI jitters faded and focus returned to the hot consumer and wholesale price inflation prints. The two-year was up 3.2 basis points to 4.77%. The 10-year yield jumped five basis points to 5.15%, and the 30-year rate advanced 4.8 basis points to 5.49%.

The relationship between Ukraine and the US is facing increasing strain over intelligence sharing, sanctions, Ukrainian attacks on Russian energy and the path to peace, CNN reported. Over the weekend, Kyiv launched one of its biggest drone attacks this year on Russia, hitting a key oil terminal, in defiance of President Donald Trump's demand that Ukraine stop hitting Russian refining plants, per the news report.

The front-month West Texas Intermediate crude oil contract jumped 2.3% to $103.77 per barrel, and global benchmark Brent edged down 0.5% to $109.36 per barrel.

title: Update: Tech-Heavy Nasdaq Leads Wall Street's Relief Rally Ahead of Key Earnings
detail:
PREMIUM
Update: Tech-Heavy Nasdaq Leads Wall Street's Relief Rally Ahead of Key Earnings
MT Newswires
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 3:42 PM CDT 3 min read
^IXIC
NVDA
GOOG
^DJI
^GSPC
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
stocks market trading wall street equity -Shutterstock

(Updates with market moves at the end of the day, and other changes, if any.)

The Nasdaq Composite rose Monday in a relief rally following last week's technology-led sell-off, as traders prepared for earnings reports from big Wall Street names, including Meta Platforms (META).

The tech-heavy Nasdaq climbed 1.1% to 26,430.89, while the S&P 500 gained 0.4% to settle at 7,690.73. The Dow Jones Industrial Average edged down 0.1% to 51,966.03. Most sectors were in the red, led by utilities, while consumer discretionary paced the winners with a 2.7% advance followed by tech's 1.2% gain.

Amazon.com (AMZN) was up 5%, the best performer on the Dow, followed by IBM and chip-making giant Nvidia (NVDA), with Alphabet (GOOG, GOOGL) also among the index's biggest gainers.

Nvidia said it ran a record-breaking quantum computing simulation on Jupiter, Europe's first exascale supercomputer, allowing researchers to explore and validate magic state cultivation.

Alphabet likely saw "relatively healthy" Google search revenue growth in the third quarter, driven by higher pricing amid solid search volume, Deutsche Bank said Monday.

On the S&P 500, SanDisk (SNDK), Datadog (DDOG) and Marvell Technology (MRVL) were among the biggest gainers.

Ameriprise Financial (AMP) fell 4.1%, among the worst performers on the S&P 500, after BofA Securities downgraded the company's stock to underperform from buy.

Netflix (NFLX) is expected to report quarterly earnings on Tuesday, with Facebook and WhatsApp parent Meta and electric vehicle manufacturer Tesla (TSLA) scheduled to release theirs on Wednesday after market close.

GE Aerospace (GE), Philip Morris International (PM), Thermo Fisher Scientific (TMO), Procter & Gamble (PG) and American Express (AXP) also report this week.

Oppenheimer Asset Management upgraded its S&P 500 full-year earnings outlook, saying the third-quarter reporting season got off to a solid start. The firm continues to expect the index to close 2026 out at 8,100.

"Our expectations are that another better-than expected quarter is in the offing," Oppenheimer Asset Management Chief Investment Strategist John Stoltzfus said in a report Monday. "Given the economic and corporate fundamentals experienced over the course of recent quarters along with watershed innovation that has seen reports of increased adoption of (artificial intelligence) by businesses and consumers, stocks may well have further upside ahead before year-end."

Treasury yields were higher with the 10-year rate up 4.2 basis points at 5.14%, while the two-year rate rose 3.4 basis points to 4.77%.

West Texas Intermediate crude oil advanced 2.1% to $103.56 a barrel in Monday late-afternoon trade, while Brent dropped 0.5% to $109.37.

US President Donald Trump on Friday signed an executive order to waive key sanctions and tariffs on Russia.

Trump had recently lifted sanctions on Russian diesel exports.

Meanwhile, Russian President Vladimir Putin has proposed a meeting between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping and himself next month to discuss a potential deal to end the Ukraine war, The Wall Street Journal reported, citing people familiar with the discussions.

Spot gold fell 0.6% to $4,140.61 per troy ounce, while silver ticked down 0.1% to $57.25 per ounce.

title: Schwab's dividend ETF drops 6% into a familiar zone
detail:
Schwab's dividend ETF drops 6% into a familiar zone
Damilola Esebame, Celine Provini
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 3:23 PM CDT 5 min read
SCHD
^GSPC
Trade SCHD on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

The Schwab U.S. Dividend Equity ETF (SCHD) bounced back after sharp declines during the 2020 pandemic crash and the 2022 market crash.

SCHD reached $35.31 on Aug. 24, 2026, before pulling back to $33.26, a roughly 6% retreat that mirrors past recoverable drawdowns, The Motley Fool reported.

Since its launch in October 2011, SCHD has delivered an average annual return of 13.11%, including periods of market turmoil during the pandemic and the 2022 bear market. 

The fund charges a 0.06% expense ratio and, as of Oct. 12, 2026, manages more than $111 billion in net assets, making it one of the largest dividend-focused exchange-traded funds.

Also Read: Schwab SCHD draws $679M as dividend ETF climbs 2.39%

SCHD still triples the S&P 500's yield after 15 years

The yield gap between SCHD and the broader market is the main reason retirees and income investors hold the fund. SCHD currently pays a 30-day Securities and Exchange Commission yield of 3.23%, more than triple the S&P 500's 1.04%, The Motley Fool reported.

Quarterly distributions have grown from $0.12 per share in late 2011 to about $0.26 in early 2026, doubling shareholder payouts, according to 24/7 Wall St.

That growth tracks the Dow Jones U.S. Dividend 100 Index, which selects companies based on cash flow, debt levels, return on equity, dividend yield, and dividend growth over five years.

Only companies with at least 10 consecutive years of dividend payments qualify, a requirement designed to favor established dividend-paying businesses, 24/7 Wall St noted.

Over the past year through October, SCHD has delivered a total return of roughly 23.4% by net asset value. 

That gain outpaced the S&P 500 over the same period as investors rotated toward dividend-paying value stocks through much of 2026, the Motley Fool confirmed. 

For investors calculating how much income SCHD can generate each month, the lower entry price means every new dollar deployed earns a higher starting yield.

Defensive sector tilts cushioned a 2022 loss to just 3.2%

Healthcare and consumer staples together account for more than 40% of the fund's holdings, giving SCHD a defensive lean absent from the S&P 500. According to the SCHD product page, healthcare represents 20.72% of the portfolio, consumer staples 20.38%, and energy 14.07%.

That sector mix limited the damage during the most recent bear market, when SCHD posted a total return loss of just 3.23% in 2022. The S&P 500 fell 18.1% in 2022 on a total return basis, a gap of nearly 15 percentage points in SCHD's favor, The Motley Fool reported.

Image from Pixabay

Arista Networks (ANET) stock trades at 55.1 times the company's earnings over the last twelve months, compared with 22.9 times for the S&P 500. A price that high acts as a bet that Arista's profits will keep growing fast for years. Anyone stepping in now is also buying after a recent decline. The shares fell 11.3% in the month to October 16, while the S&P 500 rose 0.35%. So what does that price buy you?

Arista Networks Is Outgrowing The S&P 500 Fourfold

At that price, buyers get a business whose sales are expanding well beyond the broader market. Arista's revenue grew an average of 26.2% a year over the three years to June 30, 2026, against 5.9% for the S&P 500.

Management noted during the fiscal Q2 2026 call that growth for the quarter came from its AI and enterprise customers. Anyone holding the stock is largely paying to see how long those customers keep spending.

A move like this matters most when Arista Networks is a large share of what you own. See how to protect a concentrated position.

Is Arista Networks Still Speeding Up?

The latest results indicate the pace is still accelerating. Arista's revenue growth against a year earlier rose every quarter, climbing from 27.5% in fiscal Q3 2025 to 37.7% in fiscal Q2 2026.

Management expects more. During the fiscal Q2 2026 call, executives raised their forecast for 2026 revenue to about $12.6 billion, up from $11.5 billion in May. While that figure remains a forecast rather than a final result, it marked the company's third increase of 2026.

The company has also expanded its client base. Management said its Etherlink switches for AI networks now have more than 100 customers in total. That is up from the initial four or five the company spoke of in 2024, meaning Arista now sells its AI switches to far more than the handful of buyers it started with.

What Could Keep Arista Networks From Shipping More?

A shortage of parts presents an ongoing headwind, and management does not expect it to end soon. When asked about supply during the fiscal Q2 2026 call, executives said the industry would have a two-year problem and did not expect to get out of it until 2028. They also stated that supply stays tight across the industry while component costs rise.

Arista's response has been to buy ahead. Its multiyear purchase commitments rose about 2.7-fold, rising from $3.6 billion a year earlier to about $9.7 billion at the end of fiscal Q2 2026.

Stock buyers may be betting that those commitments will let Arista keep shipping while parts stay short. The downside risk is just as specific: a shortage that lasts until 2028 may cap how much Arista can ship, and the company may earn less on what it does ship as component costs rise.
